players.product: OSAT (incl. JCET STATS ChipPAC Korea) - package substrate buyer from Simmtech and Daeduck Electronics

quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 results (annual report): revenue RMB 38,871,348,331.23, up 8.09% YoY; total profit RMB 1,738,293,696.95, up 5.42%; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 1,565,238,036.45, down 2.75%; net profit excluding non-recurring items RMB 1,369,472,054.89, down 11.51%; operating cash flow RMB 4,652,212,168.20, down 20.26%. Main-business (chip packaging and test) gross margin 13.95%, up 1.07 points. Quarterly revenue: Q1 RMB 9,335,146,486.99, Q2 RMB 9,270,077,569.34, Q3 RMB 10,063,748,622.38, Q4 RMB 10,202,375,652.52; quarterly net profit attributable: Q1 RMB 203,363,562.72, Q2 RMB 267,421,705.14, Q3 RMB 482,963,225.04, Q4 RMB 611,489,543.55. The company says domestic demand recovery and domestic semiconductor substitution lifted sales at its China plants and total revenue, while sharply higher international commodity prices pressured some raw-material costs and new plants still in product introduction and capacity ramp (not yet at large-scale mass-production revenue), plus higher finance costs, weighed on profit in the short term.

Revenue mix (annual report): 2025 revenue by end application - communications electronics 36.4%, consumer electronics 23.6%, computing electronics 21.3%, automotive electronics 9.6%, industrial and medical electronics 9.1%; computing electronics revenue grew 42.6% YoY, industrial and medical 40.6%, automotive 31.7%. By region: domestic (China) sales RMB 8,275,687,693.94, up 22.38%, gross margin 20.40% (+6.58 points); overseas sales RMB 30,438,500,306.11, up 4.62%, gross margin 12.20% (-0.47 points). Overseas factories (wholly owned subsidiaries) had 2025 revenue RMB 22,556,250,152.46 and net profit RMB 764,116,642.30; overseas assets were 36.11% of total assets.

quarterly_data.signal: Top-5 customers (annual report): sales to the top five customers were RMB 1,896,932.80 ten-thousand, 48.80% of 2025 sales; names not disclosed; related-party sales among them 0%. The company reports no single customer above 50% of sales and no new customer among the top five.

quarterly_data.signal: Top-5 suppliers (annual report): purchases from the top five suppliers were RMB 1,102,793.36 ten-thousand, 38.85% of 2025 purchases; names not disclosed; related-party purchases among them 0%.

R&D (annual report): 2025 R&D spending RMB 2,085,525,811.35 (all expensed), up 21.37%, 5.37% of revenue; 3,948 R&D staff, 15.82% of headcount. The report says 2025 R&D centred on high-performance computing, next-generation system-in-package (SiP), high-reliability automotive electronics and power/energy: multi-chip heterogeneous integration packages moved into scaled mass production with a widening customer base; CPO products delivered customer samples; glass-substrate R&D made progress, with initial validation of glass substrates for large-size FCBGA; panel-level high-density packaging (PLP) is being developed ahead; automotive e-drive modules passed certification by international mainstream auto-parts makers. For 2026 the company says it will keep raising R&D in advanced packaging and push breakthroughs and gradual adoption in 2.5D/3D packaging, ultra-large devices, high-end panel-level packaging, glass substrates and co-packaged optics.

Advanced packaging status (annual report): the XDFOI chiplet high-density multi-dimensional heterogeneous integration process series has entered mass production and is used in high-performance computing, AI, 5G and automotive applications; the company reports substantive progress in pushing 2.5D advanced packaging into mass production and in capacity release at JCET Microelectronics (Jiangyin); it has more than ten years of large FCBGA packaging-and-test experience with ultra-large-size FCBGA engineering and mass-production capability. In memory it packages and tests DRAM and Flash, with 32-layer flash stacking and 25um ultra-thin die capability, and says it works closely with the world's top three memory makers (not named). The company states it made breakthrough progress in high-end chip business cooperation with major customers (not named).

Co-packaged optics (annual report): JCET's CPO solution uses advanced packaging to integrate the optical engine with switch or compute ASIC chips on the same substrate; a silicon photonic engine developed on its XDFOI platform has completed customer sample delivery and passed validation, and the company is working with multiple customers (not named) on packaging integration, thermal management and reliability verification. Customer samples and validation only - no volume shipment stated.

Power and energy packaging (annual report): the company says it has completed the packaging innovation and mass production of a 2.5D vertical VCORE power module built on SiP technology, and has a full-chain packaging-and-test solution for 800V high-voltage DC (HVDC) data-center architecture; in 2025 it supported multiple leading international customers (not named) through sampling and end certification for 800V HVDC and, in its words, entered the supply chain of that future architecture; it delivered embedded-package samples to multiple customers and worked with a customer on GaN HEMT chip heat dissipation for humanoid robots.

Plants and utilisation (annual report, 2025 subsidiaries): STATS ChipPAC Management (Singapore) revenue US$172,278.97 ten-thousand, net profit US$12,728.35 ten-thousand (lower, on new global operations centre and R&D spending); JCET Advanced Packaging (Jiangyin) revenue RMB 215,810.49 ten-thousand, net profit RMB 58,539.29 ten-thousand - customer demand up, orders full, utilisation higher; the acquired 80%-owned flash-memory packaging-and-test plant Shengdie Semiconductor (Shanghai) revenue RMB 362,081.16 ten-thousand, net profit RMB 24,310.42 ten-thousand - some raw materials in tight supply and utilisation down; JCET Microelectronics (Jiangyin) high-end advanced packaging products in mass production with utilisation starting to ramp, revenue RMB 20,427.63 ten-thousand, net loss RMB 19,158.45 ten-thousand; JCET STATS ChipPAC Korea orders fell on the international environment with low utilisation; Chuzhou plant utilisation kept rising and it turned profitable. JCET Automotive Electronics (Shanghai Lingang) was in its build-out period in 2025 and completed line-through by year-end; the company says it will accelerate product mass-production introduction in 2026.

quarterly_data.signal: Capex and construction in progress (annual report): cash paid for fixed and other long-term assets RMB 6,298,299,227.33 in 2025, up 37.19%; construction in progress RMB 3,894,315,261.29 at end-2025, up 36.37%, mainly capacity investment at JCET Automotive Electronics and JSCK (Korea) and headquarters R&D investment. Major projects: JCET automotive chip packaging-and-test project, budget RMB 8,000,000,000.00, cumulative investment 8.53% of budget (self-funded); wafer-level microsystem integration high-end manufacturing project, budget RMB 3,800,000,000.00, 88.01% of budget. Raised-fund projects: the 10-billion-units-a-year communications high-density hybrid IC and module packaging project reached its intended usable state in December 2025 (plant built, capacity expanded) and generated total profit of RMB 4,916.05 ten-thousand in 2025; the 3.6-billion-units-a-year high-density IC and SiP module project completed plant construction and part of its equipment purchase, with RMB 210,000.00 ten-thousand of its raised funds redirected to acquiring 80% of Shengdie Semiconductor.
quarterly_data.figure: capex cash RMB 6,298,299,227.33 (+37.19%); CIP RMB 3,894,315,261.29; automotive project budget RMB 8,000,000,000.00, 8.53% invested

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 business plan (annual report, company guidance, no numeric target): the company says it will vigorously develop high-end advanced packaging and 'speed up catching up' in customer binding, technology R&D and capacity expansion, with domestic and overseas footprints to add capacity flexibility; strengthen advanced bonding, substrate/interposer material evolution, thermal and power co-design and PLP scale manufacturing for five applications (high-performance computing, AI, automotive, power and energy, storage); in automotive focus on autonomous driving and power electronics and raise the automotive plant's utilisation; at home focus on high-performance computing, AI and automotive customers; overseas 'steadily advance' advanced packaging capacity, while reducing single-source supply risk.
